The right-hand byte of each row of block $A5, written by melt_redraw.

The last byte of the VIC bank at $4000-$7FFF, which the VIC shows in the open border while idle: torture_start and torture_leave set it to $FF, the rescue screen to 0.

Cold and warm start vectors for the KERNAL's cartridge test, both $AF6A (memory_wipe), followed at $8004 by the signature CBM80 ($C3 $C2 $CD $38 $30). Every level and chamber file carries them, so a reset while the chamber is in memory runs memory_wipe and erases the game.

The chamber's 15 objects' starting x and y (30 bytes), copied to obj_xy by torture_start; objects_start_msb adds 256 to object 9's x, and the raster routine for the bottom of the screen puts objects 11-13 past 255 itself. 0-3 the four little flyers (231,44), hidden until the ball monster lets them out; 4 the ball monster on the top ledge (236,48); 5 the green monster hanging on the chain (32,112); 6 and 7 its two little hoppers (34,108); 8 the operator at the ram's lever (248,122); 9 the tub of green slime beside him (304,122); 10 Chuck's legs, left standing on the floor when he is shot (53,205); 11 and 12 the gunner's gun, placed by gunner_step; 13 the gunner (292,203); 14 the gun's muzzle flash (246,204).

The starting colours of objects 0-14, copied to obj_colour: grey for the flyers and the gun, green for the ball monster, the hanging monster and the tub, light red for the hoppers, the operator, Chuck's legs, the gunner and the flash. The three bytes after it ($804E-$8050) are not read.
The chamber's entry point: loader_hand_over jumps here once a torture chamber's file is in (part digit "3"), and the JMP goes on to torture_begin.
Set by melt_fumes after the fourteenth round of the operator's fumes: the main loop goes to the rescue screen (unless Clyde is dying).

Set by hanger_hit when a hit sends out the two hoppers; while it is set hanger_hit ignores shots. hanger_shake clears it when both hoppers' frame scripts have run out, and hopper_hit when the second hopper (object 6) is killed.
Set by hanger_shake once the monster has shaken twice and let both hoppers go: from then on only the hoppers move.
hanger_shake's index into hanger_shake_frames, 6 down to 0, twice over.

Set by baller_hit at the start of a round: the four flyers come out (flyer_round). Cleared when the last flyer (object 0) is killed or its frame script runs out; baller_hit ignores shots while it is set.
Set by flyer_round once all four flyers are out: the ball monster stops shaking. $8068 is not used.
The four flyers' places in flyer_dx and flyer_dy, objects 0 to 3.
flyer_round's index into baller_shake_frames, 6 down to 0, as the ball monster shakes the flyers out.
The four flyers' places in flyer_frames, objects 0 to 3, counted down from $4E; 0 means the flyer is gone.
flyer_round's count, 3 down to 0: a step every fourth frame.
Flyers still to come out in this round: 4 down to 0 (object 3 first, object 0 last).

Set (to 9) by baller_dead_start when the ball monster takes its last hit; ball_monster_burst then plays its burst and, when the burst ends, brings on the ball. ball_fall clears it once the ball has landed.

ball_monster_burst's count, 3 down to 0: a step every fourth frame.
ball_fall's place in ball_fall_dy.
Set to $FF by ball_fall when its script ends. Nothing reads it.
Set by ball_push_right when the flame pushes the ball from its left: ball_swing runs the ball's swing out and back, and cleared at its end.
ball_swing's place in ball_swing_dx and ball_swing_dy, from 2.

ball_roll's place in ball_roll_dx and ball_roll_dy, from 2.
0 while the tub stands (tub_bubble), $0F once the ball has knocked it over and the slime spreads (slime_flow), $FF when the slime has reached the operator: lever_cycle then stops him.
lever_cycle's count, 7 down to 0: the operator's next frame every eighth frame.
lever_cycle's index into lever_frames, lever_x and lever_char_lo, 5 down to 0, once for each pull of the lever.

operator_stop's index into operator_stop_frames.
operator_stop's count, $1E down to 0: a step every 31 frames.
Set (to 5) by lever_cycle at the end of each pull: ram_step moves the ram a pixel and clears it.
Set to $FF by ram_step when the ram is out as far as it goes and Chuck is off the ledge: the lever, the gunner's idle glances and the ram all stop.
The columns of the ram's shaft still to draw: 10 at the start, one less each time the ram's head has moved 8 pixels; below 0 the ram is out (ram_out, chuck_falling).
Counted down on alternate frames by ram_step; each time it reaches 0 (every 512 frames) Chuck's frame changes between $E5 and $E4.
Set by operator_stop as the operator stands still: melt_fumes then lets the white fumes rise and sinks him.
melt_fumes' count, $0C down to 0: the operator sinks a row every thirteenth frame.
melt_fumes' count, 3 down to 0: the fumes' next frame every fourth frame.

Rounds of the fumes' frames; at the fourteenth, rescued is set.
How far the operator has sunk inside his sprite, 0 to $14 (20 rows).

gunner_idle's index into gunner_idle_frames, $0F down to 0, one step every fourth frame.

chuck_fall's place in chuck_fall_dy.
Set to $FF by chuck_fall when Chuck lands: the gunner's script (gunner_step) and Chuck's death (chuck_doom) run, and the flame no longer moves the ball.
The gunner's state for this step (gunner_step stores it); nothing reads it.

Hits on the hanging monster that sent out hoppers, 0 to 4; with 4 the next hit kills it.

Hits taken by object 7.

Set when object 1 is killed: only then is object 0 tested against shots.
Set when object 2 is killed: only then is object 1 tested.
Set when object 3 is killed: only then is object 2 tested.
A countdown the main loop runs while it is positive, going to retry_screen without taking a life when it passes 0. torture_start sets it to $FF and nothing else writes it, so it never runs.
The three bands' ninth x bits, copied to obj_x_msb: only the second band's $80, object 9 (the slime tub) past x 255.
The three bands' multicolour bits, copied to sprite_mc_bands: all $FF.
The starting background-priority bits for sprite_behind_bands: none behind.

Sets the chamber up (also after a lost life, from retry_screen): clears the variables $8054-$80C4, puts the operator's sprite back whole (melt_redraw with A = 0), sets the bands' ninth x bits, multicolour and priority, copies the screen from screen_map ($97E2) into the screen at $4400 with each character's colour from char_colours, and sets the engine for a chamber ($126C, $1216, $120C, shot_y_max $CF, Clyde's dying count $ED, player_x_min $18 and limit $41, object_collisions' slot settings $12DE and $12E6), the ram (ram_columns $0A, so eleven columns of shaft to come, its head at x $B3, y $9D), Chuck and his two sprites from chuck_start, the colours, the 15 objects, Clyde at (176,117) in the brick tunnel; starts the tune and the raster chain at raster_panel.

Operand of the LDX at $8149: the screen copy's page count, 3 down to 0, stored at $8131. Then the rest of torture_start: shot_y_max $CF, Clyde's dying count $ED, the flags $120C, $126C and $1216 set, $12E6 = 3, the ram's settings (ram_columns 10, ram_head_x $B3, ram_head_y $9D, the band's y expansion $80), chuck_start copied, sprite multicolours dark grey and yellow, character multicolours light red and dark grey, background light blue, player_x_min $18 and player_x_limit's second byte $41, the objects, Clyde's x $B0, y $75, colour light red and all three of his sprites multicolour, his sprites blank, $7FFF $FF, the music hooks, the tune (tune_start) and the raster chain (irq_install with $01 = $36), from raster_panel at line $F9.

The chamber's main loop, once a frame: RUN/STOP pause, the weapons tablet or Clyde (player_control, player_fire, player_animate, panel_anim), then unless paused the puzzle's routines, player_dead or the touch and shot tests, the music, and the end: life_lost or the end of Clyde's dying count takes a life (below zero is game over, through torture_exit), rescued goes to the rescue screen.

The puzzle, unless paused: objects_save_positions, tub_bubble, gunner_idle, hanger_shake, flyer_round, ball_monster_burst (and ball_fall), ball_swing, ball_roll, slime_flow, lever_cycle, melt_fumes, ram_step, chuck_fall, gunner_step, chuck_doom, hit_flashes, flyer_flashes; then player_dead while Clyde is dying, or else touch_tests and shot_tests for both of his shots (X = 0 and 2).

The end of the frame's work: tune_start again whenever the tune has ended, music_frame, panel_colours_slow; retry_countdown (never armed); a lost life (life_lost, or Clyde's dying count $1288 run out) takes one from lives and goes to retry_screen, or to torture_exit when none are left; rescued, with Clyde not dying, goes to rescue_screen.
Set to $5B by torture_start; nothing reads it.
Starts the chamber's tune (torture_tune at $9CCA); the main loop calls it again whenever the tune has ended.

Raster routine at line 0: sprites_band1 puts objects 0-4 (the flyers, or the ball, and the ball monster) on sprites 3-7; Clyde's sprites 0-2 are blanked and then set by clyde_sprites, his shot sprites 1 and 2 double width and single-colour while he is dying (for the death bubble); sprite 7 (the ball monster) double height, sprite 3 blank until raster_object_0. Next raster_object_0 at line $31.
Operand of the LDA at $8324: the double height bits of raster_objects_a ($D017), $80 for sprite 7, the ball monster; torture_start writes $80 again.
Raster routine at line $31: sprite 3 shows object 0 from here down, so the ball comes into sight out of the ledge's top edge. Next raster_objects_b at line $5C.

Raster routine at line $5C: sprites_band2 puts objects 5-9 (the hanging monster, the hoppers, the operator and the slime tub) on sprites 3-7; double width from the operand at $835B and multicolour from the operand at $8365, Clyde's shot sprites single-colour while he is dying; no double height. Next raster_chuck at line $94.
Operand of the ORA at $835A, the band's double width bits: 0 from torture_start, $30 from tub_tipped (sprites 4 and 5, the fumes and the slime).
Operand of the ORA at $8364, the band's multicolour bits: $FF from torture_start, $CF from tub_tipped (sprites 4 and 5 single-colour).

Raster routine at line $94: sprite 7 shows the ram's head (frame $B3, light blue) at ram_head_x and ram_head_y; sprites 0-2 take the sparks, the blood and Chuck from chuck_xy and chuck_frames (the loop runs four times, its last pass writing harmlessly into the unused VIC registers $D0FE and $D0FF and a pointer that sprite 3 overwrites), red, red and light red; sprites 3-6 take objects 10-13 (the blood pool, the gun and the gunner), the last three past x 255; y expansion from the operand at $83DC, multicolour for sprites 2-7, no double width for 0-2. Next raster_flash at line $B4.
Operand of the LDA at $837C: the ram head's x, $B3 from torture_start, moved a pixel left at each pull of the lever (ram_step).
Operand of the LDA at $8381: the ram head's y, $9D.
Operand of the LDA at $83DB, the bottom band's double height bits: 0, and 2 (sprite 1, the blood fountain) from chuck_shot_start.
Raster routine at line $B4: sprite 7 now shows object 14, the gun's muzzle flash (position, frame and colour). Next raster_panel at line $E1.

The starting positions and frames of the three sprites raster_chuck puts on 0-2, copied to chuck_xy by torture_start: the sparks at (81,205) and the blood at (67,173), both blank, and Chuck at (169,157) in front of the ram, frame $E5.
The x and y of sprites 0-2 below line $94: the sparks of the bullets here, the blood fountain at $841E, Chuck at $8420.
The sparks' y.
The blood fountain's x and y.
Chuck's x: ram_step pushes him a pixel left at each pull, chuck_fall and chuck_moves move him on.
Chuck's y, $9D on the ram's ledge until he falls.
The frames of sprites 0-2 below line $94: the sparks here, the blood fountain at $8423, Chuck at $8424.
The blood fountain's frame.
Chuck's frame: $E5 or $E4 on the ledge, $E6-$E8 as he falls, chuck_script's frames on the floor, $EF and remains_frames when he is shot.

Raster routine at line $E1 (and the chain's first, at line $F9, where irq_install starts it): no sprite priority or double height, the score panel's sprites (panel_sprites, or panel_sprites_tablet while the tablet is up), and frame_divider. Next raster_panel_lower at line $F4.
Raster routine at line $F4: panel_lower (after two NOPs for timing) and on to raster_border; while the tablet is up, nothing until raster_border at line $F9.
The bottom border: raster_open_border, Clyde's colour back to light red ($0A) unless the fire button's charge is building, and one added to the frame flag $120D. Next raster_objects_a at line 0.
Where tub_bubble restarts in tub_bubble_frames: 9, or $0B for a second set (tub_bubble_set is always 0, so only 9 is used).

The slime tub's frames, read from the end: $C0 up to $C9 as the bubbles rise (from index 9). The second set from index $0B, $DC down to $D2 with a $FF (index 10, keep the frame) before running on into the first, is never used here.
Every fourth frame the slime tub (object 9) shows its next frame from tub_bubble_frames, round and round, until the ball knocks it over (slime_state).

The ball has hit the slime tub (ball_roll's $FE): hides the hoppers (objects 6 and 7), sets slime_state to $0F so that slime_flow runs, shows the tub at frame $D2, puts the white fumes (object 6) at (244,122) and the slime (object 7) at (248,122) by the operator's feet, in white and green, makes sprites 4 and 5 of the middle band double width and single-colour (the operands at $835B and $8365), and sets slime_step to 9.
The slime's frames (object 7), read from the end by slime_flow: blank twice, then $DD to $E3 as the puddle spreads along the ledge to the operator.

While slime_state is $0F, every fifth frame: the tub (object 9) takes its next frame up to $DB, tipping over and pouring (the steps to $D3, $D4 and $D5 also move it four pixels left), and the slime its next frame from slime_frames; after the last, slime_state becomes $FF and lever_cycle stops the operator.
The hanging monster's frames as it shakes, read from the end by hanger_shake: $95, $95, $94, $94, $95, $95, then $96 (index 0), its frame at rest.

The hoppers' frames, read from the end by hanger_shake, from index $48 (object 6) or $4C (object 7): a speck ($85), growing ($86-$88) into a hopper that bounces ($89-$8C, round and round), shrinking back from index $0D ($88 down to $85) and gone ($0F, indexes 0-9). A hopper moves only while its index is $0D or more.
The two hoppers' starting places in hopper_frames: $48 for object 6, $4C for object 7.

The handler for a shot on the hanging monster (object 5): the shot is spent; nothing happens while its hoppers are out (hoppers_out) or while it shows light red (dying). After four hits that sent out hoppers (hanger_hits), the next kills it (hanger_dying 9); otherwise, while it is green (its flash over), the hit counts, flashes it (hanger_flash 6), clears both hoppers' counts and positions and sends them out: hoppers_out, hanger_delay 1, hoppers_left 2, hanger_shake_step 6, objects 6 and 7 blank at (34,108).
The LDA of the hoppers' y, $6C (108). The label is the engine's: scroll_draw_column and scroll_finish_column read the levels' tile table at $8609, and a chamber never scrolls.
The fifth hit: hanger_dying is set to 9, and hit_flashes plays its burst.

While hoppers_out is set: every fourth frame the hanging monster shakes (hanger_shake_frames, twice), and halfway through each shake a hopper drops out (object 7, then object 6, at its place from hopper_starts and frame $85); then each hopper still alive takes its next frame from hopper_frames. When both hoppers' places reach 0, hoppers_out is cleared. Every frame the hoppers that are out move (from $8695).
The opcode of the frame loop's branch, rewritten by hanger_shake: BPL ($10) runs the loop for both hoppers, BNE ($D0) for object 7 alone, which is how it runs while the monster is still shaking.

The hoppers' moves, every frame: each hopper alive and at index $0D or more in hopper_frames moves right by hopper_dx and down by hopper_dy at its own place, which runs on by one each frame; at the end of hopper_dx ($FF) it stays there and the hopper creeps a pixel right every other frame.
Operand of the LDY at $86BC: the hopper's offset from object 6's position at $C26B (0 for object 6, 2 for object 7).
The hoppers' x steps as they leap out of the hanging monster to the right: 3s and 2s, then smaller, then 0, 30 pixels in all; $FF (index $1A) ends it.
The hoppers' y steps over the same leap: 0 for five steps, then 1, 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2: nine pixels down to the tunnel's floor, then 0.
Two bytes of hopper_dy (0). The label is the engine's: scroll_column reads the levels' row pointers at $8709 and $870A.
The end of hopper_dy: 0, 0, 0, then $FF at $870D, so the y stays put once the leap is done. The label is the engine's, as $8709's.

The handler for a shot on the ball monster (object 4): the shot is spent; nothing happens while its flyers are out (flyers_out) or while it shows light red. With three rounds won (baller_rounds), the hit kills it (baller_dead_start). Otherwise, while it is green, the hit flashes it (baller_flash 6), clears the four flyers' places, hits and dead flags, and starts a round: flyers_out, baller_delay 1, flyers_left 4, baller_shake_step 6, objects 0-3 blank and grey at (231,44).
The branch's offset. The label is the engine's: scroll_column and the Get Ready strip ($3B56) read the levels' first map row at $8715.

While flyers_out is set: every fourth frame the ball monster shakes (baller_shake_frames, its frame round and round until all four are out) and halfway through each shake a flyer pops out (object 3, then 2, 1 and 0, at $4E in flyer_frames and frame $85); each flyer still alive takes its next frame from flyer_frames; when object 0's place there reaches 0 the round is over, won or not (flyers_out cleared). Every frame the flyers that are out move (from $87E2).
The CPY's operand, 0: only object 0's script ends the round. The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip ($3B69) reads the levels' second map row at $87D5.
The flyers' moves, every frame: each flyer alive and at index $0D or more in flyer_frames moves left by flyer_dx and down by flyer_dy; at the end of flyer_dx it creeps a pixel left every other frame.
Operand of the LDY at $8809: the flyer's offset in obj_xy (0, 2, 4 or 6).
Operand of the SBC at $8812: the flyer's x step, written from flyer_dx (or $1219 at its end).
The flyers' x steps leftwards as they leap from the ball monster: 3s and 2s, then smaller, 37 pixels in all, then 0; $FF at $884C ends it.
The flyers' y steps over the same leap: 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, then up to 3 a step, 26 pixels down in all, then 0; $FF at $886F.
The ball monster's last hit: baller_dying and baller_burst_step 9, its colour light red ($C121), and baller_dead set, so that shot_tests moves on to the ball.

Once object 0 is the ball (frame $97), ball_fall instead. While baller_dying: every fourth frame the ball monster takes the next frame of burst_frames and each step scores (score value 9, 3 in the tens digit: 30 points, 270 in all); after the last, once object 0 is blank (the last flyer gone), the ball appears: objects 0 and 5 both become it (ball_appear).
The high byte of the STA's address (baller_burst_delay). The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip ($3B75) reads the levels' third map row at $8895.

Makes object X (sprite data offset Y) the ball: frame $97, x $A0, y $1C, grey. ball_monster_burst calls it for object 0 and for object 5, the hanging monster's slot, so that the ball has a copy in the middle band as well as the top one; ball_roll keeps the two together.

$0F, the byte before burst_frames. Nothing reads it: hit_flashes reads the hanging monster's burst at $88DB plus hanger_dying, but only while that is 9 down to 1, from $88E4 ($F8) down to burst_frames' blank $0F at $88DC.
The burst every creature here dies in, read from the end: $F8 to $FF, then $0F (blank) at index 0.

The ball's drop onto the top ledge, a step a frame: object 0's y moves by ball_fall_dy (bit 7 set moves it up); at the end ($FF) ball_landed is set and baller_dying cleared, and the ball waits for the flame.
Operand of the SBC at $8903: the step up, from ball_fall_dy without bit 7.
The ball's drop from y $1C: 3, then eight steps of 5 to y $47 on the top ledge, then bounces of 17 and 7 pixels ($80 and up go up), back to $47; $FF ends it.

The ball's x steps when the flame pushes it to the right (ball_swing): 4 and less, rolling up the slope at the right; then back down, to $8994; $FF at $8998 ends it. It stops 8 pixels right of where it began.

ball_swing_dx from its 24th step, as the ball slows on the slope, turns at the 41st and rolls back, to the $FF at $8998. The engine also reads this address: the Get Ready strip ($3B81) takes the levels' fourth map row from $8955.
The ball's y steps over the same swing: 0 for eleven steps, then up the slope ($81 and $82, up 16 pixels in all) and down again; $FF at $89F3.

The ball's x steps when the flame pushes it to the left (ball_roll): 5 and less leftwards ($85), up the slope at the top left to x 58, then back to the right, faster, along the top ledge, over the rise past x 255 and down the slope to the slime tub: the $FE at $8AAE is where it hits the tub (tub_tipped). It ends at $8AB7 ($FF), the ball at (309,121) where the tub stood.

ball_roll_dx from its 34th step, the ball near the top of the left slope: it stops, rolls back to the right, gathering speed, and on to the $FE and the $FF at $8AB7. The engine also reads this address: the Get Ready strip ($3B8D) takes the levels' fifth map row from $8A15.

The ball's y steps over the same roll: up the left slope ($81 and $82), down it again, up the rise on the right and down to the tub's ledge at y 121; the $FE at $8B72 is the hit, and $FF at $8B7B the end.

ball_roll_dy from its 30th step, near the top of the left slope: down it, up the rise on the right and down to the tub, to the $FF at $8B7B. The engine also reads this address: the Get Ready strip ($3B99) takes the levels' sixth map row from $8AD5.
25 bytes ($8B7C-$8B94) that nothing in the chamber reads.
$B6, a level's end scroll position in the engine (scroll_column, object_kill and game_frame_music read it here); a chamber does not scroll, so nothing in it uses this byte.

$80, the first character Clyde can pass through: the engine's movement and landing code compares the cells under and beside Clyde with it ($2CC4, $2D1A, $2D95, $2DDA, $2DFB, $2E44, $31BE and $AD1A in player_dead), and that code runs in the chamber too, so characters below $80 are the chamber's floors and walls (the engine's tests treat a character as solid when it is below this one; chamber 2's torture_leave has put them the right way round again).
The dot-matrix sign's sprite colour on the rescue screen, set every frame by raster_rescue_top from matrix_colours ($A44C); on a level the engine's level_colours_next reads its table here.
The dot-matrix sign's first sprite multicolour ($D025), set by raster_rescue_top from matrix_mc1 ($A454).
The dot-matrix sign's second sprite multicolour ($D026), set by raster_rescue_top from matrix_mc2 ($A45C).
raster_rescue_top's row counter for the sign: 5 at the top, counted down by raster_rescue_row as it moves the sprites down a row.
The ball monster's frames as it shakes out the flyers, read from the end by flyer_round: $CF, $CF, $D0, $D0, $CF, $CF, then $CE (index 0), its frame at rest.
The flyers' frames, read from the end from index $4E: a speck ($85) growing ($86-$88) into a flyer that flaps ($8D-$90), shrinking back from index $0D and gone ($0F, indexes 0-9).
Part of flyer_frames. The label is the engine's: level_colours_next reads a level's colour table here.
Part of flyer_frames, its last 18 bytes. The label is the engine's: level_colours_next reads a level's second colour table here.
The flame has hit the ball from its left: ball_swinging set and ball_swing_pos 2.
While ball_swinging: a step of ball_swing_dx and ball_swing_dy each frame (ball_move).
The LDY #0 of the x step. The label is the engine's: level_band_routines reads a level's routine table here.
The flame has hit the ball from its right: ball_rolling set and ball_roll_pos 2.
While ball_rolling: a step of ball_roll_dx and ball_roll_dy each frame (ball_move).
The BEQ that ends ball_roll while ball_rolling is clear. The label is the engine's: level_section_from_scroll reads a level's section table here.
The LDY's operand: 0, so the x step comes first. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.

The high byte of the first JSR's address (ball_move). The label is the engine's: stage_start reads a level's table here, the scroll position at which the level's opening ends for each section Clyde can restart from.
The low byte of the second JSR's address (ball_move). The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's strip length here.

Moves the ball by one step (A) of a script, x when Y is 0 and y when Y is 1: below $80 it is added, $80 and up (the low seven bits) subtracted, and the result stored in object 0 and in object 5 (the ball's copy, so the two match from the first push); a carry out of the x flips both objects' ninth x bits. $FF ends the script (ball_swinging and ball_rolling cleared, so the flame can push again) and $FE is the hit on the slime tub (tub_tipped).
The store of the new position. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The BCC. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The ball has crossed x 256: its ninth x bit flips in both bands ($C25B for object 0, $C25C for object 5).
The EOR's operand, $08: object 0's ninth x bit in obj_x_msb. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The high byte of the LDA's address ($C25C, the second band's ninth x bits). The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The RTS after a step forward. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
$FF ends the script; $FE goes to tub_tipped; the rest are steps the other way.
The CMP's operand, $FE. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
A step back: the low seven bits are subtracted. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
The LDA of the position for a step back. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's spawn section table here.
Operand of the SBC at $8C6E: the step without bit 7.
The low byte of the STA's address (obj_xy). The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's spawn section table here.
The offset of the BCC to $8C49: a borrow flips the ninth x bits. The label is the engine's: get_ready reads a level's table here.
$FF: both scripts stopped.

The operator works the lever while the ram is not yet out: every eighth frame his next frame from lever_frames, his x from lever_x and the lever's characters (lever_draw), six steps (48 frames) to a pull; at the end of each pull ram_push is set (5) and he starts again, unless the slime has reached him (slime_state $FF), when operator_stopped is set and from then on operator_stop runs instead.
Draws the lever for step X: three rows of three characters from the picture at lever_char_lo/hi into the screen at $4582 (row 9, columns 26-28).
Low byte of the LDA operand at $8CD7, the lever picture's address, moved on three bytes a row.
High byte of the lever picture's address.
The ADC #3 that moves the picture's address on a row. The label is the engine's: timer_reset reads a level's table here.
The STA's address ($8CD8). The label is the engine's: level_begin reads the address of a level's per-frame routine here (level_frame_call).
The BCC. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_player_call address here.
The INC of the picture's high byte. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_jump_call address here.
The high byte of the INC's address. The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_anim_call address here.
The screen offset moved on a row ($2B less the three written). The label is the engine's: level_begin reads a level's level_hook_call address here.
The ADC's operand. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's strip colour here.
The TAY. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's second strip colour here.
The row count's LDX, its operand at $8CF5 stored by lever_draw. The label is the engine's: raster_ready_strip reads a level's third strip colour here.
Operand of the LDX at $8CF4: the rows left, 2 down to 0. The label is the engine's: the Get Ready strip code ($3B63) reads a level's colour table here.
The operator's x for each step of a pull: $FF, or $FD (two pixels back) at step 2 as he leans on the lever.
The operator's frames for each step of a pull, read from the end: $A3, $A2, $A1, $A0 (the lever right down), $A1, $A2.
Low bytes of the lever's picture for steps 0-5 and for the lever at rest (6): $8D1D, $8D26, $8D2F, $8D26, $8D1D, $8D14, $8D38.
High bytes of the seven pictures, all $8D.
The lever's five pictures, nine characters each (three rows of three, $FD a blank): $8D14, $8D1D, $8D26, $8D2F and $8D38 (at rest).
operator_stop's steps: $A4 (he lets go), 0 (operator_melting set; on at once to) $A4, then $A5, the picture melt_redraw sinks.
Every 31st frame the operator's next step from operator_stop_frames: $A4 with the lever drawn at rest, a 0 that sets operator_melting, and $A5, where it stays.
The LDA of the next step. The label is the engine's: get_ready fills the screen with a level's character from here.
The LDA's address. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup reads a level's tune address, low byte, here.
The LDA's address, high byte. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup reads a level's tune address, high byte, here.
The BEQ for the 0. The label is the engine's: game_frame_music reads a level's end tune address, low byte, here.
The BEQ's operand. The label is the engine's: game_frame_music reads a level's end tune address, high byte, here.
The store of the operator's frame. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's animation script table (low bytes) here.

While operator_melting: every thirteenth frame, once he shows $A5, the operator sinks a row inside his sprite (melt_redraw, twenty calls, the last putting the picture 19 rows down); every fourth frame the fumes (object 6) take their next frame from fumes_frames, and at the fourteenth round rescued is set.
The fumes. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's animation script table (high bytes) here.
The white fumes' frames as the slime melts the operator: $AB, $AC, $AD once, then $A7, $A8, $A9, $AA, $A6 round and round.
Copies operator_picture into sprite block $A5 ($6940) from row A down, to the block's end: the picture moves down A rows and the rows above it keep the blank top row of the last copy.
The first ADC of A times 3. The label is the engine's: object_spawn and object_set_type read a level's third animation table here.
The operator's whole picture, 21 rows of three bytes, that melt_redraw copies into sprite block $A5; its first row is blank.
The middle byte of each row of operator_picture.
The right-hand byte of each row of operator_picture.
operator_picture from the last byte of row 6. The label is the engine's: object_kill and object_spawn read a level's colour cycle table (low bytes) here.
operator_picture from the last byte of row 11. The label is the engine's: object_kill and object_spawn read a level's colour cycle table (high bytes) here.
operator_picture from the last byte of row 16, to $8E2C, and a byte (0) at $8E2D that nothing reads. The label is the engine's: object_kill reads a level's third colour cycle table here.

Each frame, unless the ram is out (ram_out), the ball is rolling (ball_rolling) or object 0 is at y $4D or below (the ball, once it has rolled off the top ledge): on alternate frames chuck_fidget_delay counts down, and every 256 counts (512 frames) Chuck's frame flips between $E5 and $E4. Each time ram_push is set (a pull of the lever) it is cleared and the ram's head and Chuck move a pixel left; at every eighth pixel of the head the shaft grows by a column behind it, from ram_columns ($0A down to 0: columns 21 to 11 of rows 13-15). With ram_columns below 0 the ram is out: ram_out and chuck_falling are set and Chuck falls (chuck_fall).
The address of ram_out in the first LDA. The label is the engine's: object_kill reads a level's death movement table (x) here.
The STA's address, Chuck's frame ($8424). The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_path read a level's death movement table (y) here.
The high byte of the DEC's address (ram_columns). The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_10 read a level's y movement script table (low bytes) here.
The branch for X 8-10 (columns 19-21) lands inside the BIT at $8E86, on its operand: A0 00, LDY #0. X 4-7 take Y = 1 (the BIT hides the LDY) and X 0-3 Y = 2.
The middle row's character for the column. The label is the engine's: object_kill, object_spawn and hit_response_10 read a level's y movement script table (high bytes) here.
The ram is fully out (ram_columns below 0): ram_out and chuck_falling both $FF, and Chuck falls off the ledge.
The shaft's characters for row 13, by Y: $08 for columns 19-21 (X 8-10), $FD for columns 15-18, $FD for columns 11-14. Rows 13 and 15 are coloured $08 in every column.
The shaft's characters for row 14, by Y: $09, $06, $04.
The shaft's characters for row 15, by Y: $0A, $07, $05.
The colour of row 14's characters, by Y: $0B, $0B, $08.
Chuck's drop from the ram's ledge, a step a frame: 0s and 1s, then 1s and 2s, 2s and 3s, 3, 4 and 4, 48 pixels in all (y $9D to $CD, the floor), 29 steps; $FF at $8ED2 ends it.
chuck_fall_dy from its 11th step. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's wake-delay table here.
chuck_fall_dy's last three steps (3, 4, 4) and its $FF. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's table here.

While chuck_falling, a step a frame: Chuck's y moves down by chuck_fall_dy and his x a pixel left on every other frame (frame_divider's $1219); his frame steps on by one at the first step, the fifteenth and the end: $E6, $E7 and $E8 from his usual $E5 (one lower each if the fall catches him on his fidget frame $E4). At the $FF he is on the floor: gunner_firing is set ($FF) and chuck_falling cleared, and the gunner's script (gunner_step) and chuck_doom start.
The BMI's offset. The label is the engine's: object_spawn reads a level's table of hits needed (obj_hit_need, $2201) here.
The high byte of the STA's address (chuck_falling). The label is the engine's: ride_parent reads a level's y offset table here.
For each of the gunner's states 0-10, how far left of him (object 13's x) the first piece of his gun (object 11) goes: $18, $18, $1A, $11, 8, 8, then 0 for the states without the gun.
gun_a_dx from state 3. The label is the engine's: object_kill compares the object it is killing with a level's end object here ($149D).
For each state, how far above the gunner's y the gun's first piece goes: 0, 0, 9, $11, $18, $12, then 0.
For each state, how far left of the gunner the gun's second piece (object 12) goes: 0, 0, 4, 7, 8, 8, then 0.
For each state, how far above the gunner the gun's second piece goes: 0, 0, 2, 1, 3, and $83 for state 5, where bit 7 puts it 3 below instead; then 0.

The gunner's frame (object 13) in each state: $B4 holding the gun in states 0-4, $CB as he brings it round (5); without it $BC (6), $BD, his mouth open (7), $BE and $BF turning away (8, 9) and $CA, his back turned (10).
The gun's first piece in each state: $AE and $AF level (0, 1), $B5, $B7 and $B9 rising towards upright (2-4), $CC as it comes round (5), then blank ($0F).
The gun's second piece in each state: $B0, $B1, $B6, $B8, $BA, $CD, then blank.
How many frames each state lasts, less one: 1, 1, 3, 3, $50, 2, $50, $35, 4, 4, $35.

The gunner's states in order. gunner_step moves on before it reads, so index 0 is never used. He stands facing out (6) for 81 frames, opens his mouth (7), turns his back (8, 9, 10) and turns round again (9) with the gun (5), which he holds upright (4) for 81 frames and lowers to level (3, 2, 1). Then each $FE plays the two entries before it 26 times over: he aims for 104 frames, fires 26 shots (state 0 has the muzzle flash, state 1 not), holds his fire for 104 frames, fires 52 more, and raises the gun again (2, 3, 4). The $FF costs Clyde the life, about 18 seconds after Chuck landed.
The script's $FF: gunner_script_pos steps back so the $FF is read again, and life_lost goes up, which the main loop acts on at once (a life lost and the Get Ready screen, or the game over).

While gunner_firing: runs gunner_script, one state a time. When gunner_delay runs out the next entry is read; a state (0-10) sets the gunner's frame (object 13, gunner_frames) and the two pieces of his gun (objects 11 and 12: gun_a_frames and gun_b_frames, placed by gun_a_dx, gun_a_dy, gun_b_dx and gun_b_dy from his position), and gunner_delay from gunner_delays. State 0 shows the muzzle flash (object 14, frame $B2) and every other entry blanks it. $FE goes back two entries until it has been met 26 times (gunner_repeats); $FF stays and sets life_lost.
The BNE for any state but 0 lands inside the BIT at $8FA3, on its operand: A9 0F, LDA #$0F, so the flash is blanked; state 0 takes LDA #$B2, the flash.
An LDA of gun_a_dy that the next LDA overwrites; it does nothing.
While gunner_firing, each frame: sparks_moves (where the bullets strike), chuck_remains (once he has been shot) and chuck_moves (Chuck's own script).

Runs chuck_script for Chuck's sprite: a byte of $80 and up is his next frame; one below $80 is a wait of that many frames; $FE moves Chuck, the sparks and the blood fountain a pixel left and reads on; $FF stops.

Runs sparks_script for sprite 0, the sparks where the bullets strike: a byte of $80 and up, or $0F (blank), is the sprite's next frame; any other byte below $80 is a wait of that many frames; $FE is the burst that cuts Chuck in two (chuck_shot_start); $FF stops.
Below $80: $0F is a frame, anything else a wait.

Chuck on the floor after his fall: $E8 for 72 frames, $EC for 6, $EB for 165, $E9 for 12, then $9F (a frame of Chuck kept away from his others at $E4-$F2) for 148; then he shuffles left a pixel at a time ($FE, $EC for 7 frames, $EB for 5) eight times, waits ($EA for 32, $EB for 64, $EA for 16), shuffles three times more and stops at the $FF at $90FC.

The bullets' sparks on Chuck: nothing for 402 frames (four waits), so they start as the gunner's first burst of fire does; then eight bursts of sparks ($F3-$F7, a frame each, with 8 blank frames after), 36 blank frames, a low spray (sparks_spray), 16 blank frames, three more bursts, the $FE that cuts Chuck in two, 8 blank frames and the $FF at $9195.
sparks_script's low spray at Chuck's feet: frames $91, $92, $93 and $D1, four frames each, four times over (to $917C).

sparks_script's $FE, the bullets cutting Chuck in two: chuck_shot set; his legs (object 10, frame $ED) appear at (53,205), their place from the start, about where his shuffle has brought him; his own sprite shows his top half ($EF) at y $C6; the blood fountain (sprite 1) is made double height ($83DC = 2) and the sparks move to (46,212).

While chuck_shot, each frame: Chuck's top half drops by remains_dy and, where remains_dx is set, moves a pixel left, toppling through remains_frames until it shows $F2; after 36 steps it lies still. Every third frame the blood fountain (sprite 1) takes its next frame from blood_frames and the sparks (sprite 0) theirs from remains_sparks, both round and round; every fourth frame the legs (object 10) flip between $ED and $EE.
The blood fountain's frames, round and round: $9E, then $98-$9D; $FF goes back to the start.
The sparks' frames after the shot: blank ($0F) for 13 steps, then $F3-$F7; $FF goes back to index $0D, so the sparks go on until the scene ends.

Whether Chuck's top half moves a pixel left at each step of chuck_remains: every other step from the third, sixteen pixels; the $FF at $926C is only tested for nonzero, so it moves it a 17th time, and the 36th step reads remains_dy's first byte (0).
How far Chuck's top half drops at each step: nothing for 22 steps, then 1s and 2s, 15 pixels in all; the $FF at $9291 ends the slide.
The top half's frames as it topples: $F0 for seven steps, $F1 for five, then $F2, which chuck_remains keeps.
Until the ram is out, the gunner fidgets: every 200 frames he steps through gunner_idle_frames from index $0F down to 0, a step every fourth frame.
The gunner's idle frames, read from index $0F down to 0: $BB, $BB, $BC, $BC four times, ending on $BC (the two frames differ only in their bottom rows). The 17th byte ($92E3) is not read.

The rescue screen's dot-matrix sign, a byte for each of its seven rows (the top at $92EA): each bit lights one of the eight sprites in its row. matrix_scroll fills it a letter at a time from matrix_font.
The sign's top row (matrix_rows + 6), which raster_rescue_top shows first.
"CLYDE HAS SAVED CHUCK FROM" and $FF: print_at's string 5, the rescue story's first line.
"BEING SHOT TO PIECES" and $FF, string 6.
"CHUCK OFFERS CLYDE HIS COLLECTION" and $FF, string 7.
"OF MAGIC POTION CREATURES AS REWARD" and $FF, string 8.
"WITH A SIGH OF RELIEF CLYDE ACCEPTS" and $FF, string 9.
"THEM, REALIZING HIS QUEST IS COMPLETE" and $FF, string 10: in this chamber the story ends the game.
"RESCUE CHUCK AS SOON AS POSSIBLE" and $FF, string 11: the Get Ready screen's line.

Puts back the engine settings torture_start changed, on the way out (torture_exit): the panel's and the tablet's sprites to y $DD, $126C cleared, $24F0 and $7FFF set to $FF, object_collisions' slot settings ($12DE 0, $12E6 0, $12EA 8), player_x_min $1F, the second byte of player_x_limit (past 255) $3B and shot_y_max $BF.

Puts Clyde on sprite 0 (position, pointer and colour) and his two shot sprites on 1 and 2 (positions from $1290, pointers $128D and $128F, colours), the ninth x bits of all three into $D010 beside the band's own, the second sprite multicolour ($D026) yellow, and all eight sprites on. raster_objects_a calls it each frame.

Clyde's collisions, each frame he is not dying: the handler is touch_handler, which kills him; the box is his own (player_box_x, player_box_y). Tested, unless blank or bursting ($F8 and up): the hanging monster (hanger_test, not while it is the ball's copy), the two hoppers, the ball monster (baller_test, its y 15 lower) and the four flyers, object 0 not while it is the ball ($97).
Tests the hanging monster (object 5) with the box A picks (0 Clyde's, 1 the shot's), unless it is blank, bursting ($F8 and up) or the ball's copy ($97).
Tests the object at x A, y X and frame Y with the box chosen: test_setup, then test_object. hanger_test and baller_test end here, and flyer_tests and ball_test call it.
Tests the ball monster (object 4) at its x and its y plus 15 with the box A picks, unless its frame is blank or $F8 and up.

Each frame, for the hanging monster and its hoppers. While hanger_dying is set, the routine runs only every fourth frame, and then the monster (object 5) first takes the next frame of its burst, $88DB plus the count from 9 down to 1 ($F8 to $FF, then blank $0F), in light red; at 0 the count stays, so the INC of hanger_dead at $955F is never reached. Then its flash after a hit (hanger_flash_colours), each hopper's flash (hopper_flash_colours) and, every third frame, each hopper's burst (burst_frames, from hopper_burst_step).
How many hits each hopper takes before the killing one: $0A for object 6, 8 for object 7 (hopper_hit counts in hopper_hits). Object 6 dies on its 11th counted hit, object 7 on its 9th.
A hopper's colours after a hit, read from index 5 (the first byte of hanger_flash_colours) down to 0: orange, purple, blue, purple, orange, then light red, its own colour, again.
The hanging monster's colours after a hit, read from index 6 down to 1: white, white, light green, light green, cyan, then green, its own colour. Index 0 (orange) is the hoppers' first flash colour.

The handler for a shot on a hopper (X from the operand at $95AF): the shot is spent; while the hopper shows light red (its flash over) the hit counts in hopper_hits and flashes it (hopper_flash 5), and once hopper_hits_needed is reached it bursts instead (hopper_burst_step 8, light red, hopper_dead set); killing object 6, the second out, ends the round (hoppers_out cleared).
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $95AE: which hopper the shot hit, 0 for object 6 and 1 for object 7, written by hopper_tests.
Tests the hoppers for a shot, in the order they must die: object 7 (the first out) unless blank or dead, and object 6 only once object 7 is dead; hopper_hit learns which through the operand at $95AF.
test_setup and then test_object, the same two calls as test_at, for hopper_tests.

Each frame, for the ball monster and its flyers: the monster's flash after a hit (baller_flash_colours), each flyer's flash (flyer_flash_colours) and, every third frame, each flyer's burst (burst_frames, from flyer_burst_step).
How many hits each flyer (objects 0-3) takes before the killing one: 7 each, so each dies on its 8th.
A flyer's colours after a hit, read from index 5 (the first byte of baller_flash_colours) down to 0: white, white, light green, light grey, light grey, then grey, its own colour.
The ball monster's colours after a hit, read from index 6 down to 1: white, white, light green, light green, cyan, then green. Index 0 (white) is the flyers' first flash colour.

The handler for a shot on a flyer (X from the operand at $966B): the shot is spent; while the flyer is grey (its flash over) the hit counts in flyer_hits and flashes it (flyer_flash 5), and once flyer_hits_needed is reached it bursts (flyer_burst_step 8, light red, flyer_dead set). Killing object 0, the last out, wins the round: baller_rounds goes up and flyers_out is cleared.
Operand of the LDX #$FF at $966A: which flyer the shot hit, 3 down to 0, written by flyer_tests.

Tests the flyers for a shot, in the order they must die: object 3 (the first out) unless blank or dead, then object 2 once object 3 is dead, object 1 once object 2 is, and object 0 once object 1 is; flyer_hit learns which through the operand at $966B.

Tests the ball (object 0), from shot_tests. It leaves the box choice (the operand at $97AB) as the last test set it, which is always the shot's: hanger_test and hopper_tests set it to 1 earlier in shot_tests, since hanger_dead is never raised and shot_tests always runs them. Were object 0's frame 0, it would run on into touch_handler; the chamber never gives it that frame.
touch_tests' handler: JMP $3CEC, into player_hurt past its invulnerability tests, so a touch kills Clyde whatever.

The tests for Clyde's shot X (0 or 2, shot sprites 1 and 2), when it is not blank. Unless hanger_dead is set, which never happens: the hanging monster (hanger_hit) and the hoppers (hopper_hit). Until baller_dead: the ball monster (baller_hit) and, unless object 0 is the ball, the flyers (flyer_hit). Once the ball monster is dead, or object 0 is the ball: the ball (ball_hit, ball_test).

The handler for the ball: nothing while gunner_firing. With the flame out ($1235 negative), Clyde facing left ($122D) pushes the ball left (ball_push_left) unless it is already rolling, and facing right pushes it right (ball_push_right) unless it is already swinging. Any other shot is spent, so bullets stop at the ball.
JMP test_object ($4C $C9 $97), which nothing reaches: it follows ball_hit's JMP to shot_spent.

Puts the object under test (A = x, X = y, Y = frame) in the spare slot 15 ($C27D, $C27E, $C179), the only one object_collisions tests in a chamber, clears zero page $3D and $3E, and sets the box: Clyde's (player_box_x, player_box_y) when the operand at $97AB is 0, otherwise shot $43's (shot_box, shot_box_y).
Operand of the LDA #$FF at $97AA: which box test_setup sets, 0 for Clyde's, otherwise the shot's; hanger_test, baller_test, hopper_tests and flyer_tests store A here, ball_test does not.

Runs object_collisions for slot 15 with its ninth x bit ($C25E) and its tall bit ($C009) clear: it zeroes the AND operands at $97D5 and $97DB itself before using them, so an object past x 255 (the ball, far out on its swing) is tested as if it were 256 pixels further left.
Operand of the AND at $97D4, zeroed by test_object on every call: slot 15's ninth x bit.
Operand of the AND at $97DA, zeroed the same way: slot 15's tall bit. Then object_collisions.

The chamber's screen, 25 rows of 40 character codes: torture_start copies four whole pages from here into the screen at $4400, so the last 24 bytes it copies ($9BCA-$9BE1, the start of char_colours) land in the unused bytes and sprite pointers at $47E8-$47FF before the sprites are set.
The colour RAM value of each of the chamber's 256 characters: torture_start colours every cell of the screen by the character in it.

The chamber's own tune, different from the first two chambers', started by tune_start (music_play with $9CCA), in the music driver's format: a header of two voice offsets ($55 and $140, from the first voice), the three voices' streams from $9CCE, $9D23 and $9E0E, and the nine sections they call, $A00F to $A0DF.
torture_tune's first voice, to its end command at $9D22: settings and section $A086 six times over.
torture_tune's second voice, to $9E0D, almost all calls: 29 of them, to sections $A00F, $A018, $A02B, $A03A, $A045 and $A052 in a changing order.
torture_tune's third voice, to $A00E: sections $A067 and $A0BD, $A052 four times, $A067 and $A0BD again, then $A052 twelve times.
The last fifteen bytes of torture_tune's third voice (it crosses $A000 here): its last settings and notes, and the end command ($1E) at $A00E.
The nine sections torture_tune's voices call (music command $23), each ending in a return ($24): $A00F, $A018, $A02B, $A03A, $A045, $A052, $A067, $A086 and $A0BD, the last ending at $A0DF.
Fills both screens with character $FF, a blank, and the colour RAM with black (screen_fill with X = $FF and A = 0), and sets 40 columns.
memory_swap 6: exchanges the text character set with the chamber's, for the Get Ready and rescue screens.
The chamber's first start, reached from the entry at $8051: weapon_setup with X = 0 and Y = 0 (weapon 0 at grade 0, the panel's icon set by loader_hand_over), then retry_screen.

The Get Ready screen before each try: clears the engine's variables $120C-$126C and sets $126D-$1272 to $FF, swaps in the text characters (inverted by charset_invert), draws the lives digit, the score and GET READY, moves the panel and tablet sprites down to y $ED, points print_at's strings 5-11 at this file's texts and prints string 11, "RESCUE CHUCK AS SOON AS POSSIBLE", at $4683, starts sound effects $15 and $16, and runs the colour bars (raster_retry_bars). Fire on joystick port 2 silences it, blanks the screen, puts the characters back and starts the chamber (torture_start).

The colour bars' sixteen colours, read from the end, so from the top down: brown, red, orange, light red, light grey, yellow twice, white, light green, cyan, green, light blue twice, purple, dark grey and blue. The same colours as the other two chambers' Get Ready screens.
A second copy of retry_bars_a; raster_retry_bars takes one or the other on alternate frames, so the bars stay the same.
Low bytes of retry_bars_a and retry_bars_b, picked by frame_divider's $1219.
High bytes of the two colour lists.

The Get Ready screen's raster routine at line $69 (line $F9 the first time, where irq_install starts the chain): sixteen lines of background colour from the list for this frame (delays from colour_bar_delays); then the background and the second sprite multicolour yellow, and the lives sprite (sprite 0, block $4E, Clyde's face, light red, at x $A9, y $9D, its ninth x bit clear), shown or hidden with frame_divider's $121B so it blinks every four frames. Next raster_retry_panel at line $E0.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $A1FA, the colour list's address, from retry_bars_lo.
High byte of the colour list's address, from retry_bars_hi. The code after it writes the bars, sets the lives sprite and counts the frame for retry_screen ($120D).
The Get Ready screen's line $E0: panel_sprites. Next raster_retry_lower at line $F4.
The Get Ready screen's line $F4: panel_lower and the open border. Next raster_retry_bars at line $69.
Low bytes of the seven texts at $92EB-$93AB (rescue_text_1 to rescue_text_7), copied into print_at's strings 5-11.
High bytes of the seven texts: $92 for the first, $93 for the other six.

The rescue: plays rescue_tune and shows the dot-matrix sign spelling WELL DONE, its dots little pictures of Clyde's face. Every other frame two colour lists rotate a place: the big letters take the first list's front colour and the six story lines take successive places of the second, so the colours ripple down them. After $78 counts every other frame (about five seconds) it prints WELL DONE in big letters, the six lines of story and the potion digit 6; potion_award then counts the digit down, paying potions. Fire leaves (torture_exit).

The STY that moves the old last colour of well_done_colours to the front. The label is the engine's: player_dead reads five water characters from $A300 on levels 1.1 and 1.2 only, and player_hit_object a table of harmless frames from stage 6 on, but a chamber's main loop never calls player_collisions.
The STY's address. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup writes $32 here on world 2's levels; a chamber starts at its own entry ($8051) and never runs stage_main_setup.
The high byte of the STY's address. The label is the engine's: world 2's levels have a routine here, called by stage_main_setup and player_hit_world2; the chamber runs neither.
The STA's address, story_colours. The label is the engine's: player_hit_object jumps here for frame $8F from stage 6 on, but the chamber's main loop never calls player_collisions.
The fourth story line's screen page ($45). The label is the engine's: level_player_call's operand still holds level 3.2's $A39A, but torture_start sets $126C, which skips that call.
Prints big string 14, the potion digit at $ABF3, at $470B.

Leaves the chamber, from the rescue screen or when the last life has gone (the main loop at $82E6): silence, sprites off, a black background, a blank screen and torture_leave; with lives left it swaps the character set back and loads the next stage (stage_next), else game_restart.
The LDA #0 after the SEI. The label is the engine's: level_jump_call's operand still holds level 3.2's $A3C5, taken only while $122B is set, and retry_screen clears it.

Pays the reward, once the digit has been printed (the cell at $470B is no longer $FF) and each time the flowing colours bring dark grey ($0B) to the front of story_colours (every 40 frames): the digit at $ABF3 counts down from 6 to 0; at each step potion_add adds the worth of Clyde's last potion pickup (the ADC operand at $B8B4, 1 or 5) to the kind award_kinds names and to the total. With the usual 1 that is six potions, two of each kind.
Operand of the LDY at $A40B: the new digit (5 down to 0), the index into award_kinds.
For each step of potion_award (digit 0-5), the potion counter it pays into: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3.
rescue_screen's count before the big text appears: set to $78 and counted down every other frame.

The first of twenty colours that flow along the big WELL DONE, red at the start: rescue_screen rotates the list a place every other frame, the last ($A436) moving to the front, and this front colour goes to both rows of the big letters ($D883 and $D8AB, eighteen cells each) and the digit's top left cell ($DB0B).
The list's second colour (light red at the start), the big digit's top right cell ($DB0C).
The list's third colour (yellow at the start), the digit's bottom right cell ($DB34).

The list's fourth colour on, the first of them the digit's bottom left cell ($DB33). From the start: light red, red, blue, light blue, cyan, light blue, blue, brown, orange, light red, orange, brown, dark grey, green, light green, green.
The list's last colour, dark grey at the start, which moves to the front at each rotation.
The first of twenty colours that flow down the six story lines, white at the start: it colours the first line ($D91F, 26 cells), and potion_award pays each time it is dark grey ($0B).
The second colour, the second line ($D947, 26 cells).
The third colour, the third line ($D9BC, 35 cells).
The fourth colour, the fourth line ($D9E3, 35 cells).
The fifth colour, the fifth line ($DA5A, 37 cells).
The sixth colour on, the first of them the sixth line ($DA82, 37 cells). From the start: light green, cyan, green, dark grey, black, black, brown, orange, light red, yellow, then white.
The list's last colour, white at the start, moved to the front at each rotation.

The sign's fade step, counted down from 7 to 0 every other frame by raster_rescue_top and indexing matrix_colours, matrix_mc1 and matrix_mc2: matrix_scroll sets it to 7 six frames before each letter changes, so the dots have faded to black, or nearly, when it does.
The sign's sprite colour for each fade step 0-7: light red when settled, then orange, brown, black at steps 3-5, brown and orange.
The sign's first sprite multicolour for each fade step 0-7: dark grey when settled, black at steps 1-7.
The sign's second sprite multicolour for each fade step 0-7: yellow when settled, then light red, orange, brown, black at step 4, brown, orange and light red.

The rescue screen's top raster routine (line 0, line $F9 the first time): counts the frame ($120D) and flips frame_divider's flags itself; on alternate frames it runs panel_anim from $2A19 (past its own alternate-frame test) with the face's stage $123C at $FF and steps the fade down. Then it sets the sign's three colours for the fade step, all eight sprites multicolour and shown, none expanded, sprite 0's ninth x bit, the row count ($8B9A) 5, and puts the eight sprites in a row at y $2A (matrix_set_y, matrix_xy), all showing block $4E (Clyde's face) in the sign's colour, with the top row of matrix_rows switched on. Next raster_rescue_row at line $40.

Moves the sign's sprites down $1A lines and enables the next row of matrix_rows, six times, at the lines in matrix_lines; then raster_rescue_panel at line $E0. All sprites are behind the characters here ($D01B = $FF).
The second DEX, on to the next sprite's y. The label is the engine's: level_anim_call's operand still holds level 3.2's $A50D, taken only while $122B is set.
The rescue screen's line $E0: panel_sprites, sprites in front again. Next raster_rescue_lower at line $F4.

The high byte of the JSR's address (panel_sprites). The label is the engine's: level_hook_call's operand still holds level 3.2's $A537; a chamber runs its own main loop, not the one that makes that call.
The rescue screen's line $F4: panel_lower and the open border. Next raster_rescue_top at line 0.
Moves the sign's sprites' y in matrix_xy on by $20; raster_rescue_top calls it after placing the sprites, and matrix_set_y overwrites it the next frame, so it changes nothing on screen.
Sets all eight y positions in matrix_xy to A.
The sign's eight sprites, x and y: x $11C, then $FC down to $3C, 32 pixels apart, sprite 7 on the left.
The y positions in matrix_xy, set by matrix_set_y and matrix_next_y.
The raster lines of raster_rescue_row's second to sixth runs, read from the end: $5A, $74, $8E, $A8, $C2.
matrix_scroll's letter count, 9 down to 0, back to the font's start after the tenth.
Frames until the next letter: $16, so a letter every 23 frames.

Changes the sign's letter (each frame of the rescue screen): six frames before the change it starts the fade ($A44B = 7), and at the change copies the next seven-byte letter of matrix_font into matrix_rows, the letter's first byte into the top row ($92EA), wrapping after ten.
Low byte of the LDA operand at $A5AC, the letter's address in matrix_font, moved on seven bytes a letter.
High byte of the letter's address. Then the copy into matrix_rows and the step to the next letter.

The sign's ten letters, seven rows of eight dots each, top row first: a space, W, E, L, L, a space, D, O, N, E, which matrix_scroll copies into matrix_rows a letter at a time. The same bytes as chambers 1 and 2's.

The rescue screen's tune, played by rescue_screen (music_play with $A60B), the same tune as the first two chambers' rescues: a header of two voice offsets, the three voices' streams from $A60F, $A686 and $A6F5, and the three sections they call ($A7DE, $A7E9 and $A7F6), to $A7FC.
rescue_tune's first voice, to its end command at $A685; it calls no sections.
rescue_tune's second voice, to $A6F4; it calls section $A7DE five times.
rescue_tune's third voice, to $A7DD; it calls sections $A7E9 and $A7F6.

rescue_voice_3 from its 19th byte. The label is the engine's: object_spawn's LDA at $2082 still holds level 3.2's last movement script address, $A707; object_spawn writes it before each read, and the chamber never calls object_spawn.
rescue_voice_3 from $A747: notes between calls of section $A7E9, up to its change of settings at $A79F.
The rest of rescue_tune's third voice, from a change of settings (commands $12 and $11): notes between calls of sections $A7F6 and $A7E9, to its end command at $A7DD.
The three sections rescue_tune's voices call (music command $23), $A7DE, $A7E9 and $A7F6, each ending in a return ($24), the last at $A7FC.

From here to $ABF2, 1014 bytes that the chamber never runs or reads, the same as chamber 2's file holds at these addresses: the end of its potion_award, its colour lists, its rescue screen's raster routines, its sign's code and font and its rescue tune. The file was saved from memory that still held chamber 2 there.
chamber_2_leftovers: chamber 2's raster_rescue_row. The label is the engine's: object_spawn's LDA at $20B7 still holds level 3.2's last colour-cycle list, $A919, written again before each read.
chamber_2_leftovers: chamber 2's matrix_xy, and from $A969 its matrix_lines and matrix_scroll.
chamber_2_leftovers: the middle of chamber 2's matrix_xy. The label is the engine's: level_frame_call's operand still holds level 3.2's $A95F; a chamber runs its own main loop, not game_frame.

chamber_2_leftovers: chamber 2's matrix_font from its 42nd byte, then from $A9FF its rescue tune, to $ABF2. The label is the engine's: stage_main_setup calls a level's code here on the first two stages (see world1_ranges); a chamber never runs stage_main_setup.
print_big's string 14, the potion digit ("6", $FF), counted down by potion_award.
print_big's string 13, "WELL DONE" and $FF; the file's last byte, $ABFF ($BC), is not read.
